archetypes.name: wire-contract-parity
archetypes.rationale: This migration replaces dozens of bash scripts with Python; the most dangerous failure mode is subtle drift in stdout KV key ordering, TSV column positions, NDJSON schemas, conditional key emission (promote-latest phase sets), and exit codes — contract drift can silently break orchestration callers without a test failure.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit each new Python main function against its documented wire contract: KV key order and completeness for resolve-prs (six-key order), close-priors (TAB-separated CLOSE_FAILED rows), promote-latest (phase-conditional emission — prelude keys, DRY_RUN omission on live runs, RELEASE_ALREADY_LATEST omission on dry-run, post-edit-only RELEASE_IS_* keys), pacific-timestamp (two-key stdout, no stdout on parse failure), and map-runs TSV column order. Check that pre-selection failures in promote-latest emit no stdout at all, and post-selection failures preserve already-emitted phase KVs. Verify that exit codes match documented contracts: resolve-prs exits 0 for error-KV outcomes and 1 only for unknown argv; verify-main exits 2 only for usage errors; scan-run exits non-zero for run-dir-missing and run-dir-invalid. Confirm quiet routing is re-initialized before plugin read-version emits stdout so command substitution callers capture LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION correctly. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
